title: A Hymn for the Harvest
premise: Elodie Marchetti arrives in the dying farm town of Hollow Creek to teach its last remaining class, where students vanish one by one each autumn and the town sings an old harvest hymn to 'bring them home.' She soon learns the hymn is a covenant: the town feeds a child to the field each year, and in exchange the crops—and the town—survive. The imaginary friend who waited on her porch, a boy called Wick, is the field's previous offering, and he has been waiting thirty years for someone who can hear him. As Elodie uncovers that she was the child who escaped the covenant as a girl, she must learn the hymn's forbidden final verse—the verse that ends the bargain—at the cost of her own voice, her safety, and the town's forgiveness. In the climax she sings the last verse alone in the harvest field, freeing Wick and the taken children but dooming Hollow Creek to famine; the book ends with the town, hollowed and hungry, choosing to rebuild together rather than sing again, and Elodie, voiceless but no longer invisible, staying to teach them how.
about_author: Ulyana Almeida grew up between a Portuguese fishing village and a rust-belt American farm town, a childhood split between two kinds of hunger. Her horror fiction explores the bargains small communities make to survive, and she swears she has never once sung along.

chapters.title: The Last Class
chapters.summary: Elodie Marchetti arrives in Hollow Creek, population dwindling, to teach eleven students in a school built for two hundred. The town welcomes her with unnerving warmth and a gift basket containing a hymnal she didn't ask for. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: cautious optimism shadowed by the sense of being expected.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: On her first Friday, Elodie's roll call comes up one short—Marcus Reed is simply gone, and no one, not even his parents, seems alarmed. The principal hands her a form labeled 'Harvest Withdrawal.' POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the first crack of wrongness beneath polite small-town normalcy.

chapters.title: The Boy on the Porch
chapters.summary: At dusk Elodie finds a barefoot boy of about nine sitting on her porch steps, unchanged and unaged, calling her by a childhood nickname no one in Hollow Creek could know. Wick, her imaginary friend, has been waiting. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: terror curdling into a homesick, impossible recognition.

chapters.title: Hymn Practice
chapters.summary: The town gathers in the grange hall to rehearse the harvest hymn; Elodie attends to fit in and notices the children sing with dead eyes, and that the final page of every hymnal is torn out. Wick appears in the doorway, shaking his head. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: belonging offered at a price she can't yet name.

chapters.title: Withdrawal Slips
chapters.summary: Elodie investigates the school's records and finds forty years of 'Harvest Withdrawals'—a child every autumn, always the one nobody would miss. The oldest file bears her own surname: Marchetti, 1989, status: escaped. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: dread as the mystery turns inward.

chapters.title: What Wick Remembers
chapters.summary: Through fragments and gestures, Wick shows Elodie his last night in 1989: the field, the song, the adults' faces lit by lanterns, and a little girl pulled from the line at the last moment by her mother's betrayal of the town. POV: Elodie, with Wick's memory interludes. Emotional beat: grief for the boy who was taken in her place.

chapters.title: The Kindness of Strangers
chapters.summary: The town turns its warmth up to suffocating: casseroles, offers of help, a church deacon named Amos probing gently about whether Elodie 'remembers the old songs.' She realizes their kindness is surveillance. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: claustrophobia disguised as hospitality.

chapters.title: Second Verse, Same as the First
chapters.summary: Another student, shy Delia Okafor, stops attending. Elodie drives to the Okafor farm and finds the family mid-celebration—grief and relief tangled together, as if a debt were paid. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: horror at a community that mourns and gives thanks in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Elodie finds a pre-torn hymnal in the school basement, its final verse intact: a melody that 'unmakes the bargain,' addressed not to the field but to the ones it took. Wick refuses to come near the book. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: hope arriving as something dangerous.

chapters.title: Amos Knows
chapters.summary: Deacon Amos visits Elodie at night and reveals he knows who she is—the girl who escaped, the reason the harvests have thinned for thirty years. He offers her a choice: sing the covenant verse at this year's harvest and restore the town's fortune, or be 'withdrawn' herself. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the mask drops; the town's love becomes a threat.

chapters.title: Root Cellar
chapters.summary: Elodie discovers the school's root cellar connects to old tunnels beneath the field, and inside, small belongings—decades of shoes, lunchboxes, a hair ribbon—arranged with terrible care. The children aren't gone; they're kept. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: revulsion and a fierce, new protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Mother's Letter
chapters.summary: In her rented house Elodie finds a letter hidden by a previous tenant—her own mother's confession, explaining she saved Elodie by offering Wick's name instead, and that the debt deferred has been accruing interest ever since. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the found family theme inverts; her blood family's sin made flesh.

chapters.title: Chorus of the Missing
chapters.summary: At night the field begins to sing the hymn in children's voices, practicing, patient. Wick stands at the fence line, and for the first time he speaks aloud: the final verse must be sung by someone the field wants, or it will take the whole class instead. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the stakes crystallize—her students' lives against her own.

chapters.title: Eleven Desks
chapters.summary: Elodie tries to evacuate her students; the town seals the roads 'for the festival,' and parents gently return runaway children to her classroom, apologizing. She understands there is no leaving Hollow Creek. POV: Elodie, with a brief interlude from student Tommy's diary. Emotional beat: isolation deepens; the trap closes.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Amos forces Elodie to lead hymn practice, testing her voice against the covenant verse; when she deliberately sings flat, the crops visible through the windows wilt in real time. The town's patience is ending. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: performance as survival, and the first taste of the hymn's power.

chapters.title: What the Field Wants
chapters.summary: Wick confesses the truth: the field doesn't want a child—it wants her, the one that got away, and every vanished student was a down payment to keep her within reach. Her survival has been the town's slow sacrifice. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: guilt as the price of survival becomes literal.

chapters.title: The Night Before Harvest
chapters.summary: On the eve of the festival, Elodie and Wick memorize the forbidden final verse together in the dark, her voice and his memory, while lanterns kindle across the valley like a congregation of eyes. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: quiet, terrified tenderness—the found family of two.

chapters.title: Harvest Home
chapters.summary: The whole town gathers at the field's edge in their best clothes. The children are lined up in white. Amos calls Elodie forward to sing the covenant verse and seal the bargain—and the field itself goes silent, waiting for her. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the calm at the center of the storm.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Elodie opens her mouth and sings the torn-out verse instead—the one that releases, not binds. The field tears open, the taken children step out of the soil unaged, and Wick, finally sung home properly, begins to fade with a smile. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: climax—grief and liberation in a single breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: The covenant broken, the crops blacken overnight; the town wakes to famine and fury, some blaming Elodie, some secretly relieved. Amos is found standing in the dead field, hollow-eyed, humming a verse no one will finish. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the cost of survival paid in full, and no regrets.

chapters.title: Voiceless
chapters.summary: The last verse took Elodie's singing voice—she can speak, but never again carry a tune. She reopens the school, now filled with the returned children, and teaches them everything except the hymn. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning with what was traded away.

chapters.title: A Hymn for the Harvest
chapters.summary: A year later, Hollow Creek is smaller, poorer, and stubbornly alive, its people learning to survive without a bargain. On the first day of autumn, Elodie's students write their own song—wordless, humming, imperfect—and she stays to hear it. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging earned, not bought; found family, finally home.
